prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop portfolio landing-page direction comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design an actual responsive website viewport for COLTON SPURGIN as a flight-test debrief and engineering after-action record. Leadership and engineering must share one operating record: objective, evidence, result, next move. The visitor must quickly understand who Colton is, what he has done, and whether his working style fits them.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; this is a flat front-facing website screenshot on a continuous report sheet
Subject: a candid personal portfolio for an Air Force NCO, lead software developer intern, research assistant, and UWF senior specializing in AI who graduates December 2026 and wants to build useful ambitious software before pursuing a master’s degree
Style/medium: high-fidelity editorial web UI inspired by restrained flight-test reports, after-action reviews, instrument plots, red-pencil review marks, and excellent modern typography; quiet, confident, trustworthy, never cosplay
Composition/framing: a narrow report header with COLTON SPURGIN and WORK, EXPERIENCE, ABOUT, CONTACT; below it, a decisive opening brief in a two-column grid: left column shows “OBJECTIVE 01” and the large statement “BUILD USEFUL SYSTEMS. LEARN THE HARD PROBLEMS. LEAD THE WORK WELL.” with VIEW THE WORK and START A CONVERSATION; right column shows a compact CURRENT RECORD with AIR FORCE NCO, LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN, RESEARCH ASSISTANT, AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026. The second fold begins as a chronological debrief strip with four evidence entries: BORK, VELLM, TSP BENCHMARKS, HOME LAB, each organized by ROLE, WORK, and STATUS. Make one thin flight-path line moving through the chronology the single dominant signature geometry. Keep every other region quiet.
Color palette: report paper #eee9dc, blue-black #182026, review rust #c65335, instrument gray #7e8e91
Materials/textures: subtle onion-skin report paper, fine instrument lines, sparse red-pencil marks, monospaced annotations
Text (verbatim): “COLTON SPURGIN”; “WORK”; “EXPERIENCE”; “ABOUT”; “CONTACT”; “OBJECTIVE 01”; “BUILD USEFUL SYSTEMS. LEARN THE HARD PROBLEMS. LEAD THE WORK WELL.”; “CURRENT RECORD”; “AIR FORCE NCO”; “LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN”; “RESEARCH ASSISTANT”; “AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026”; “DEBRIEF LOG”; “BORK”; “VELLM”; “TSP BENCHMARKS”; “HOME LAB”; “VIEW THE WORK”; “START A CONVERSATION”
Constraints: this must read unmistakably as a usable desktop website, not a poster, cockpit, or military-themed game; all core UI copy legible; factual and restrained; no portrait photo; no logo; no rank insignia; no aircraft imagery; no invented employers, metrics, awards, testimonials, or project claims
Avoid: military cosplay, camouflage, flags, medals, HUD overlays, generic SaaS cards, bento grid, neon cyber aesthetic, terminal UI, 3D mockup, browser chrome, illegible pseudo-text, gradients, rounded pill buttons, heavy shadows, watermark
